historical_references.reference: According to Hindu mythology, Hrishitaa is the name of a celestial nymph (Apsara) who was in love with the sage Agastya. When Agastya left his ashram to perform tapas, Hrishitaa followed him disguised as a cow. Agastya, recognizing her true form, blessed her with the power to nourish all beings. After this, Hrishitaa is identified with the star Arcturus.

Hrishitaa was also the name of a queen of the Vakataka dynasty during the 5th century CE in India. She is known for her patronage of art, particularly temple architecture. Her most notable contribution was the construction of the temple complex at Aihole, which is considered an important site of early Chalukyan architecture.
